q: When two or more electromotive sources (batteries) are connected in series, the resultant emf is the algebraic sum of the individual emfs.
e: True. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. Series, the resultant emf is the algebraic sum of the individual emfs.

q: In series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in opposite directions.
e: False. The right claim is this: In a series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in the same direction. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. The printed line wrongly says in series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in opposite directions.

q: In series aiding, the resultant emf is $E_1 + E_2$.
e: True. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. In series aiding, the resultant emf is E1 + E2.

q: The total internal resistance of two batteries in series aiding is $r_1 - r_2$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The total internal resistance of those two batteries in series is (r1+r2). In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. The printed line wrongly says the total internal resistance of two batteries in series aiding is r1 - r2.

q: Two batteries in series aiding can be regarded as a single battery having an emf $(E_1 + E_2)$ and internal resistance $(r_1 + r_2)$.
e: True. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises. Having an emf (E1 + E2) and internal resistance (r1 + r2).

q: In series opposing arrangement, the emfs of the batteries are in the same direction.
e: False. The right claim is this: In a series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in the same direction. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. The printed line wrongly says in series opposing arrangement, the emfs of the batteries are in the same direction.

q: The resultant emf in series opposing is the sum of the individual emfs.
e: False. The right claim is this: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the difference between the individual emfs. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. The printed line wrongly says the resultant emf in series opposing is the sum of the individual emfs.

q: If $E_1$ is greater than $E_2$, the resultant emf of those two batteries in series opposing is $(E_1 - E_2)$.
e: True. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. Emf of those two batteries in series opposing is (E1 - E2).

q: The total internal resistance of two batteries in series opposing is $r_1 - r_2$.
e: False. The right claim is this: In series opposing, the total internal resistance of the two batteries is r1 + r2. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. The printed line wrongly says the total internal resistance of two batteries in series opposing is r1 - r2.

q: In parallel connection of two identical batteries, the opposite polarity terminals of the batteries are connected together.
e: False. The right claim is this: If terminals of opposite polarity are connected together in parallel, batteries may be damaged. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. The printed line wrongly says in parallel connection of two identical batteries, the opposite polarity terminals of the batteries are connected together.

q: The resultant emf of the parallel-combination of two identical batteries is just the emf $E$ of a single battery.
e: True. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. Two identical batteries is just the emf E of a single battery.

q: Since the internal resistances of two identical batteries are in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is $2r$.
e: False. The right claim is this: Since the internal resistances of identical batteries are in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is (r)/(2). Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises. The printed line wrongly says since the internal resistances of two identical batteries are in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is 2r.

q: A parallel combination of two identical batteries can be regarded as a single battery having an emf $E$ and an internal resistance $r/2$.
e: True. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. A single battery having an emf E and an internal resistance r/2.

q: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the same polarity should be connected together.
e: True. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. Taken that the terminal of the same polarity should be connected together.

q: If terminals of opposite polarity are connected together in parallel, batteries may be damaged.
e: True. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. If terminals of opposite polarity are connected together in parallel, batteries may be damaged.
